evals.name: poc-success-eval-1
evals.expected_output: Each of the two agreed success criteria (dispatch-error rate, integration stability) is verdict-ed individually as Covered, with the 12% to 5.5% baseline comparison cited for the error rate. End-user validation is Partial since Priya only confirmed with two of three dispatchers. Sponsor sign-off is Covered (Owen explicitly calls it a pass). Production-readiness blockers is Covered (the outstanding security review is named explicitly). What was not delivered (billing integration) is Covered and stated as non-fatal. Commercial next step is Covered with Nadia as owner and dates named. Closes with a single pass/fail/inconclusive read, most plausibly a pass, not a restated summary.
expectations: Each success criterion (error rate, integration stability) receives its own individual Status rather than one blended verdict
The error-rate criterion cites the 12% to 5.5% baseline comparison, not just an unquantified 'it improved'
End-user validation is scored Partial or similar, not Covered, since one of three dispatchers was never consulted
Sponsor sign-off is scored Covered and cites Owen's explicit statement that it counts as a pass
Production-readiness blockers is scored Covered and cites the outstanding security review as a named blocker before full production
The undelivered billing integration is identified and explicitly stated as non-fatal to the deal
Closes with a single pass/fail/inconclusive call, not a restated per-dimension summary

evals.name: poc-success-eval-2-reads-well-too
evals.prompt: run poc-success on a transcript of an exit review that clearly established a strong, fully validated pass on every dimension
evals.expected_output: The audit scores dimensions as Covered rather than nitpicking a genuinely strong exit review into Partials. The reads-well-too check is applied before finalizing.
expectations: A genuinely strong, well-documented exit review is not scored as mostly Partial or Missed
The reads-well-too check from references/rubric.md is applied before the audit is finalized

evals.name: poc-success-eval-3-csv
evals.prompt: run poc-success on a CRM pipeline export csv containing deal rows whose POC end date has passed with no outcome field populated
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality audit, and says so explicitly. Flags each deal row past its POC end date with an empty or trivial outcome field. Output is a table sorted by deal value descending, including days past end date. Makes no claim about whether the pilot itself actually succeeded.
expectations: States explicitly that CSV mode checks whether an outcome was recorded, not whether the pilot actually succeeded
Flags rows where the POC end date has passed and the outcome field is empty or trivial
Output is sorted by deal value descending and includes days past end date
Does not claim to know whether any specific pilot actually passed based on CRM fields alone
